lesson.title: Social scoring
lesson.summary: Apply the social-scoring test and its alternative unrelated-context and disproportionate-treatment branches.

prerequisites.reason: The scoring case must be read as a set of elements and consequence conditions.

blocks: The **social-scoring test** concerns AI evaluating or classifying people or groups over time from social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal/personality characteristics.
That evaluation must lead to specified detrimental or unfavourable treatment. A score existing alone does not establish the whole prohibition; examine what it does to people.

The first treatment branch concerns social contexts unrelated to where the data were generated or collected. Trace the source context and the treatment context rather than assuming all data use crosses this boundary.
Fictional Northbridge case: a score drawn from unrelated social conduct is used to deny a service in another context. The stipulated unrelated contexts and detrimental effect let us test this branch.
The second branch concerns treatment unjustified or disproportionate to the social behaviour or its gravity. It can matter even without an unrelated-context finding.
The branches are alternatives: either or both can satisfy this part of the test. Do not require both in every case. A relevant data context does not by itself cure disproportionate treatment.
Record evaluation over time, input characteristics, score, treatment and the applicable branch. This point is not a general prohibition on every numerical score or every credit assessment.
Other Article 5 points, high-risk classification and personal-data law can still apply when this particular social-scoring test is not established. Keep the conclusion exact.
